title: Web Development Prerequisites
description: A short baseline check of HTML, CSS, and JavaScript fundamentals — the shared prerequisite for most Learning Hub paths. Skipping this leaves your self-reported proficiency unverified.

questions.question: Which element should wrap the dominant, unique content of a web page?
questions.explanation: <main> holds the page's primary content and must not be repeated across the document. <div> has no semantics, <section> groups thematic content, and <article> is for self-contained compositions.

questions.question: Which markup gives screen-reader users a text description of an image?
questions.explanation: alt is the correct attribute for describing an image's meaning. title only adds a tooltip and is unreliable for assistive tech, description is not a valid attribute, and aria-label is meant for elements with no text equivalent at all.

questions.question: How do you horizontally centre a block-level element that has a fixed width?
questions.explanation: auto left/right margins split the remaining space equally. text-align centres inline content inside the element, align-items works inside flex/grid, and justify-self is not a valid value (it takes start/center/end).

questions.question: On a flex container, which property distributes space along the main axis?
questions.explanation: justify-content acts on the main axis. align-items works on the cross axis, align-content only affects wrapped lines, and place-items is the align-items/text-align shorthand.

questions.question: What is the key difference between display: none and visibility: hidden?
options: none keeps the space but hides the paint
none removes the element from the layout entirely
hidden removes the element from the DOM
questions.explanation: display: none removes the box, so following content reflows into the gap. visibility: hidden keeps the space occupied. Neither removes the node from the DOM.

questions.question: What is the difference between == and === in JavaScript?
options: == coerces types before comparing; === does not
questions.explanation: == converts operands to a common type first, so "1" == 1 is true. === requires both value and type to match, so "1" === 1 is false. Prefer === to avoid surprise results.

questions.question: Which declaration is confined to the block it is declared in?
questions.explanation: let and const are block-scoped. var is function-scoped and hoisted, which is why it produces surprising results inside loops and conditionals.

questions.question: What does Array.prototype.map() return?
options: A new array of the same length with transformed values
questions.explanation: map always returns a new array with one result per input element. reduce() is what accumulates to a single value, and forEach() returns undefined.

questions.question: What does event.preventDefault() do inside a form submit handler?
options: Stops the handler from running again
Stops the event bubbling to parent elements
Cancels the browser's default action (the native submit/navigation)
Removes the form from the page
questions.explanation: preventDefault() cancels the default behaviour, such as a native form submission and page reload. stopPropagation() is what prevents bubbling, and stopImmediatePropagation() also blocks other listeners on the same element.

questions.question: Which selector method returns a NodeList of every match?
questions.explanation: querySelectorAll returns all matches as a static NodeList. querySelector returns only the first match, getElementById returns one element, and getElementsByClassName returns a live HTMLCollection rather than one element.
